title: Split the area between MACs and memory
story: You have 60,000 gates of silicon for a small matrix engine: a systolic array of 8-bit MACs (608 gates each) and an on-chip SRAM buffer (1 gate per bit) between it and DRAM. DRAM delivers 2 bytes per cycle, so the array is only busy if each weight it fetches is reused across a batch of at least 32 inputs held in the buffer. For an 8 x 8 array that needs a buffer of at least 16 kbit (16,384 bits). The engine must reach 64 MACs per cycle. Choose the array (slot S1) and the buffer (slot S2).

goals.label: the buffer holds at least 16 kbit

hints: An N x N array does N^2 MACs per cycle and costs 608 N^2 gates.
Add the array's area and the buffer's bits: both must fit in 60,000.
